check_text:
protocol.py: 3 biology problems (1 error, 2 notes).

1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: mix (tube A1 in slot 2)
   line 46:  p20.aspirate(15, mix_tube)
   At line 46 the tip went into mix (tube A1 in slot 2) while it still carried template_A1 +
   water (well A1 in slot 4), template_A2 (well A2 in slot 4), template_A3 (well A3 in slot
   4), template_A4 (well A4 in slot 4) and 92 more from an earlier step (this line did it 96
   times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it
   touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from
   it then took the unwanted material along into 95 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6,
   A7, A8, A9 and 87 more in slot 3.
   Affected: tube A1 in slot 2.
   Also reached 95 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 87 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 46 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [b92bccc83814]

2. NOTE NO-SAMPLE-INTO-REAGENT-WELL: (proposed) A tip that had been in a sample went into a
reagent
   line 46:  p20.aspirate(15, mix_tube)
   At line 46 the tip touched the liquid in tube A1 in slot 2 while it still carried
   template_A1 + water (well A1 in slot 4), template_A2 (well A2 in slot 4), template_A3
   (well A3 in slot 4), template_A4 (well A4 in slot 4) and 92 more from an earlier step
   (this line did it 96 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in
   the next liquid it touches, and the protocol never transfers that liquid into this well
   on purpose. A reagent is shared: the master mix, the enzyme or the primer in that well
   goes into every reaction on the plate. A tip that has been in one sample leaves a little
   of it in the next liquid it touches, so a sample carried into a reagent well turns up in
   every well that reagent reaches, and a no-template control can no longer be trusted.
   Liquid was later taken out of the affected wells, and the unwanted material went along
   into 95 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 87 more in slot 3.
   Affected: tube A1 in slot 2.
   Also reached 95 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 87 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Use a fresh tip for each sample at line 46, or add the reagent to the wells first,
   while the tip is clean, and the samples afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [8bc853b721cc]

3. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 96 wells of mix with a sample
   line 47:  p20.dispense(15, dst)
   At line 47 the robot starts putting mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full Skirt
   (slot 3), and 96 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds
   the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is
   contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing
   on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8
   and 88 more in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 88 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 15 ul of mix and 5 ul of water in place of the
   template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [6b7eac8235aa]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

A tip that has been in one sample leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so a sample carried into a reagent well turns up in every well that reagent reaches, and a no-template control can no longer be trusted. Liquid was later taken out of the affected wells, and the unwanted material went along into 95 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 87 more in slot 3.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each sample at line 46, or add the reagent to the wells first, while the tip is clean, and the samples afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: No no-template control: 96 wells of mix with a sample
findings.explanation: At line 47 the robot starts putting mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full Skirt (slot 3), and 96 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 88 more in slot 3.
findings.fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 15 ul of mix and 5 ul of water in place of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
